# Fable V9-INT — integrated revision of V2 (parent), with V6 propeller adopted

**Status of this document.** This is a design revision by the original author, not an independent validation. Every number is one of three kinds and is tagged as such: **[DA]** design assumption (chosen, not derived), **[EC]** external calculation by a stated method from tagged inputs, **[MR]** measured result — of which there are **none** in this packet. No wind-tunnel, whirling-arm, bench or flight measurement exists for any part of this aircraft. The 1898 packet contained none of the stability theory used below; all of it is modern method applied in this feedback round.

## 1. What changed from V2 and why

The evaluator's blockers were: (a) tail/fin sweep and clearance still unresolved, (b) fuel centroid outside its own box, (c) transverse-shaft versus frame/brace interface (v1 B‑4), (d) V6/V8 propeller work not reconciled with the aircraft, (e) no whole-aircraft trim or inertia, hence no admissible mode analysis.

V9‑INT answers these by: rebuilding the tail-half attachment so the actuation horn lives outside the frame (the V2 horn tips at z 0.475 were below the lower longeron at that station, z≈0.49 — a hard clash I had not caught); redefining the fuel tank as a box with its centroid inside it and with fuel split from tank; inserting a frame station at x 1.85 so the transverse shaft passes through a bearing block rather than through the crossing point of the side-face diagonals (which cross at z 0.70, 0.10 m from a 0.80 shaft); adopting the V6 propeller geometry (D 2.3 m, 2 blades, 600 rpm, hub r 0.10 m, β table) side‑by‑side at the V2 hub positions, with the V3b 12 kg pair mass carried as a proposal; enlarging the tail to 5.0 m² and adding a removable 5 kg nose ballast provision so the nominal CG sits at 34.5 % chord with seat travel giving 33.2–35.9 %; and producing a **shape-model mass ledger** from which an inertia tensor is calculated (tagged [EC], uniform-distribution assumption, not measured). V8 material is not in this packet and is not integrated; the V6 chord table is carried as PROVISIONAL exactly as V6 labels it.

Rejected options are retained in the JSON (`rejected_options`): moving the whole wing aft 0.10 m (touches every coordinate), moving the engine forward (collides with seat travel), a 1/12 arc section (V2 rejection stands), and a continuous tail (V1 clash).

## 2. Sign and inertia conventions (used everywhere below)

Body frame B: origin at front cross-member centreline, **x aft, y right, z up** (right-handed, as V1/V2). For flight-dynamics use, the evaluator should transform to a conventional stability frame (x forward, z down) by x_s = −x, y_s = y, z_s = −z; under that map I_xz changes sign. Inertia tensor is in the **tensor (negative-product) form**: I_xx = Σm(y²+z²), I_xy = −Σm xy, I_xz = −Σm xz, about the CG, axes parallel to B. Moments: pitch positive nose-up (positive about +y in B), roll positive right wing down (positive about +x in B... note that in B, +x is aft, so a right‑wing‑down roll is a *negative* rotation about B‑x; I therefore state roll and yaw in the stability frame only: roll positive right wing down, yaw positive nose right). Controls: tail positive = TE down; rudder positive = TE left (nose right); tip panels positive = left TE down (roll right).

## 3. Trim state (V9 nominal, [EC] by the V2 simplified method, not independent)

W = 303.7 kg × 9.81 = 2979 N; V = 13 m/s; q = 103.5 Pa; S_ref = 42 m² (both decks); c_ref = 1.85 m. CL = 0.685. With CLα_w 3.8/rad and α₀ −5.7° (arc 1/20, [DA]/[MR‑method]), wing α ≈ 4.6° body. Drag [EC]: CD0 0.06 × qS = 261 N + induced ≈ 160 N + tail/fin ≈ 15 N → **~435 N**, propulsive power 5.66 kW; at an *assumed* propeller η 0.5 the shaft requirement becomes **11.3 kW** (was 10.7). Engine capability remains UNKNOWN. Tail: V_H = 5.0 × 4.49 /(42 × 1.85) = 0.289; estimated NP ≈ 43 % chord [EC]; CG 34.5 % → static margin ≈ 0.085 c nominal, 0.071–0.098 over seat travel, fuel effect < 0.1 %. Estimated trim tail deflection ≈ −1.5° (with −4° rigging), inside ±12°. This trim is *my* closure, and the evaluator's finding stands: **there is no independent admissible whole-aircraft trim**, so nothing below ranks modes.

## 4. Test/analysis matrix and root calculation path

The JSON gives the state grid (3 speeds × 3 CGs × power on/off), the full derivative list with the method for each, and the exact procedure for assembling the 4×4 longitudinal and lateral matrices and extracting roots. C_L_α̇ and C_m_α̇ are **UNKNOWN**; the only admissible route without measurement is a frequency-domain unsteady panel or an oscillating-model whirling-arm test; the lag-of-downwash formula is listed as a *bounding estimate only*. No root values are given because no admissible derivative set exists; order-of-magnitude expectations (short-period ~2 rad/s, phugoid ~6 s period) are labelled as classical approximations that are not a verdict.

## 5. If a mode is unstable

The likeliest problem is lateral: zero dihedral and a 1.62 m² fin/rudder set behind two propellers whose discs lie 1.4 m ahead of the CG (destabilizing normal force). The concrete pre-planned change is 2.5° dihedral on the lower-deck outer bays (|y| > 2.60) plus a 0.30 m² fin extension; mass, trim and power consequences are quantified in the JSON.

## 6. Verdict

UNVALIDATED. No crewed flight, no construction clearance. Go/stop criteria are numeric and listed.
